chunks: Yunus, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from Hassan al-Jammal, from Amira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The people have been commanded with recognizing us, and referring to us, and submitting to us.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And if they were to fast, and pray, and testify that there is no god except Allah, and make it within themselves that they would not refer to us, they would become, due to that, polytheists.'
ai.seo_question: Why are acts of worship insufficient for true faith according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates 'Ma'rifah' (gnostic recognition) of the Imams to the status of a divine command, asserting it as the essential criterion for true monotheism. He illustrates that ritual acts like prayer and fasting are insufficient for salvation if they are not anchored in submission to the Imams' authority, effectively rendering such worship a form of hidden polytheism (shirk) when disconnected from them. This underscores the Shia doctrine that the Imams are the living proof of God on earth, making their recognition inseparable from the recognition of God Himself.
